...SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS WEDNESDAY AFTERNOON AND EVENING OVER
IDAHO ZONES...

.Scattered thunderstorms are expected again across far
southwestern Idaho and the western Magic Valley Wednesday
afternoon. Expect gusty and erratic winds up to 55 mph in the
vicinity of these thunderstorms.

The National Weather Service in Boise has issued a Red Flag
Warning for lightning, which is in effect from 1 PM this
afternoon to 8 PM MDT this evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...In Idaho, Fire Weather Zone 424 Western Twin
Falls BLM.

* TIMING...From 1 PM this afternoon to 8 PM MDT this evening.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Scattered coverage with abundant lightning.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusty erratic winds up to 55 mph.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.

* WHERE...Iowa River at Marengo.

* WHEN...From this evening to tomorrow afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Water reaches the bottom of the levee
surrounding Marengo. Water affects low lying agricultural land
along the river

- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
late this evening to a crest of 15.1 feet just after midnight
tonight. It will then fall below flood stage tomorrow
morning.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
The Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources has issued an Air
Quality Advisory for the following counties: Kenosha, Milwaukee,
Ozaukee, Racine, Sheboygan.

WHAT...The Ozone AQI is expected to reach the Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups (Orange) to Unhealthy (Red) level.

WHERE...Southern Lake Michigan shoreline.

WHEN...From noon until 11 p.m.

Precautionary/Preparedness Actions:
Sensitive groups: Do not do long or intense outdoor activities.
Schedule outdoor activities in the morning when ozone is lower.
Consider moving activities indoors.
People with asthma: Follow your asthma action plan and keep
quick-relief medicine handy.
Everyone else: Reduce long or intense outdoor activity. Take more
breaks, do less intense activities. Schedule outdoor activities
in the morning when ozone is lower.

Additional Details:
Ozone concentrations are forecast to range from Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups (Orange) to Unhealthy (Red) AQI within the lake
breeze. The highest concentrations are expected from Milwaukee
County south to Kenosha County.

For more information on current air quality, please see:
https://airquality.wi.gov

events.summary:
FFWFWD

The National Weather Service in Fort Worth has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Hopkins County in north central Texas...

* Until 1000 AM CDT.

* At 749 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over eastern Hopkins County, mainly between Sulphur
Bluff and Saltillo. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain have fallen.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Rapid rises
to the White Oak Bayou and its tributaries are also ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Saltillo, Pine Forest, Weaver, Flora and Dike.
